english.title: Breach a section 123 restriction on the publication / distribution of an advert / information relating to child adoption
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[published an advertisement]_
(B)_[published information]_
(C)_[distributed an advertisement]_
(D)_[distributed information]_
(E)_[caused an advertisement to be published]_
(F)_[caused information to be published]_
(G)_[caused an advertisement to be distributed]_
(H)_[caused information to be distributed]_

to which section 123 of the Adoption and Children Act 2002 applied in that **(..SPECIFY NATURE OF ADVERTISEMENT OR INFORMATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 124 of the Adoption and Children Act 2002.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
published / distributed
advertisement / information
regarding child adoption prohibited by s.123

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: A person is not guilty of an offence under this section unless it is proved that he knew or had reason to suspect that section 123 applied to the advertisement or information. But this subsection only applies if sufficient evidence is adduced to raise an issue as to whether the person had the knowledge or reason mentioned

other.penalty:
Summary: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months and / or a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale

Time limit for prosecutions
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
